correctness.rationale: The published Rousseeuw--Ruts triangle depth expression is reconstructed in barycentric coordinates, where it is exactly four times the smallest pairwise barycentric product. The central-region area then reduces by sixfold permutation symmetry to two elementary integrals over one ordering chamber. Their exact evaluation gives the closed formula, and the product maximum at equal barycentric coordinates gives the extinction level 4/9. Symbolic replay verifies the integral identity and series; a separate fixed-seed numerical integration test agrees.
risks: The pointwise depth formula is published prior work and is used as a premise rather than claimed as new.
The Monte Carlo check is diagnostic only.

Candidate-specific database and public-literature searches under triangle floating-body, Tukey-depth-area, barycentric-product and logarithmic-profile formulations found no covering result.

value.rationale: The triangle is the canonical first polygonal model for convex floating bodies and halfspace depth. General polygon theory records a logarithmic small-cap law, while the statistical-depth literature records the triangle contours pointwise. Converting those contours into the exact full volume profile supplies a natural invariant at every level, identifies the extinction scale, and sharpens the asymptotic with explicit leading and lower-order coefficients.
risks: The result is two-dimensional and does not solve the higher-dimensional simplex volume-profile problem.
